title: "Task list"
---

File for discussing ideas/improvements. Your notes, then Claude's reply in 🟦 and yours in 🟧. New notes go above **Settled**; what is agreed moves there, then into the plan documents. Pasted images land in `images/` beside this file; `python3 scope.py images` deletes one once nothing mentions it (D132).

**Starting a new chat.** Paste this, with the section's heading filled in:

``` text
Work on the task list section "<heading>" in plan/tasklist.qmd.
```

That is all a new chat needs, because the rest is already written down. It reads `.claude/CLAUDE.md` by itself, which sends it to `plan/design.md` (what exists), `plan/roadmap.md` (status and what is next) and `plan/decisions.md` (why), and tells it to answer here, topic by topic, in 🟦 and 🟧. Its memory notes load by themselves too. The one rule that keeps it true: **anything that matters and was only said in a chat goes into this file before that chat ends**, under the section it belongs to, or it is lost to the next one.

## Supporting table csv issues

I still get the issue where File Column lands with quotes ('DiagnosisCode'), and this prevents the connection on the fact table. Removing the quotes fixes it so it's a minor issue for next build. I even think i saw a warning about it in validate so it must reecognise it.

![](images/paste-1.png)

![](images/paste-2.png)

::: {.callout-note title="🟦 Claude: Supporting table csv issues"}
**What the code does today.** The file's header really is `'DiagnosisCode'`, quotes included: a CSV quotes with `"`, so single quotes are part of the name. Validate says so (`quoted_column_name`, D109), and its fix is the rename you did by hand. The app shows the file's name in "Lands as" as it is, so a recipe reading `DiagnosisCode` finds nothing until the quotes are taken out.

**Recommendation.** In Supporting Tables, a file column whose name carries quotes gets a **Remove quotes** button beside it. The button writes the rename (`'DiagnosisCode'` lands as `DiagnosisCode`), visibly, in the same place you'd type it. The rename is still yours to press, as D45 wants. The warning stays for templates edited by hand. Alternatively, the app could fill in the clean name by itself, but that is the kind of guess you've preferred to make yourself.

**For you to decide:** the button, or the automatic fill?
